newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index ends bourse at all-time close.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index ends bourse at all-time close.

text.p: The German DAX index ended bourse trade on Tuesday at yet another all-time closing level, with the main inspiration behind record gains coming from the dollar's ongoing resilience.
The DAX index ended 43.59 points at 3,276.16 points in early bourse trade after reaching a new record high at 3,287.79 points, helped by the dollar climbing above 1.70 marks.
"The dollar is still the engine for the gains," said one Frankfurt trader.
But gains may be limited ahead of the afternoon when Wall Street resumes trading after the long U.S. holiday weekend.
And some traders said the market was due for a period of consolidation after the recent heady gains in a bid to make the market appear attractive again to investors.

Bank stocks were a major factor behind the market's record advance following a positive reception to results from Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, as well as the Bavarian-based Vereinsbank, which both reported higher profits.
Deutsche ended up 1.97 marks at 88.35 marks, while Vereinsbank pared early gains to end unchanged at 63.90 marks.
Construction group Philipp Holzmann AG ended up eight marks at 459 marks after saying it expected 1996 construction output to be steady at 14.1 billion marks despite the weak economy.

Trading against the trend was carmaker Volkswagen AG, which ended down 3.75 marks at 802.50 marks after Monday's statement that production would be cut due to the Spanish trucker strike interrupting shipments from parts suppliers.

VW is also again under pressure after saying on Monday that it has asked German prosecutors to investigate allegations of purchasing department officials demanding and accepting bribes from supplier to be given contracts.
Chemical shares were also in favour as BASF AG and Bayer AG both posted strong gains, with BASF up 1.05 marks at 64.20 marks and Bayer up 1.32 marks at 70.72 marks at end bourse.
